anomaly_def.Name: Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly: Sustained physical read and write demand overruns the available throughput, IOPS, or latency capacity of the underlying storage volumes, making the disk subsystem the primary bottleneck.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly: Network transport, listener, authentication, or socket-handling resources are unable to service incoming connections and data transfers at the required rate, producing client-side timeouts, retransmissions, and connection refusals.

When both conditions coexist, the database experiences a multilayer performance collapse. Disk queues, read/write latencies, and durability flush waits soar while, in parallel, connection-establishment times lengthen, sockets pile up in wait states, and application pools flood the listener with retries. End-users observe highly variable query response times, periodic stalls, and sporadic disconnects. Server metrics show moderate CPU, but extreme I/O wait, swollen session counts, backlog and accept queue saturation, increased network round-trip times, and surges of aborted transactions. Because slow storage elongates statement execution and commit phases, each session holds its network resources longer, further exhausting socket and process limits, while network retransmissions and throttling delay log shipping, replication, or backup traffic, worsening storage congestion.

Causally, saturated storage inflates I/O waits, extending transaction and result-set lifetimes; this keeps connections open, grows the active session population, and drives the listener toward exhaustion. Simultaneously, network slowdowns or connection churn force the server to buffer more result data and maintain idle backends, increasing memory pressure and dirty-page accumulation that must eventually be flushed to already overtaxed disks. The feedback loop between elongated disk operations and protracted network interactions amplifies latency at both layers, obscuring which tier is primary and pushing the database into a compounded resource starvation state.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits longer than net_write_timeout while writing a block to the client connection.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
